All forecasting experts converge in assessing this as an extremely close contest, with India and Japan's nominal GDP for 2025 neck-and-neck—IMF projections and multiple official statements indicate that India has either just surpassed or will narrowly surpass Japan, with the projected margin consistently under $2 billion out of over $4 trillion GDP. Japan's persistent stagnation, demographic decline, and yen weakness versus the USD further amplify India's prospects in this nominal (USD) GDP metric. 

The single largest uncertainty cited by all is exchange rate volatility: should the yen unexpectedly appreciate, or the rupee weaken, Japan could retake the lead in the final IMF measure. Similarly, the razor-thin margin means even a small revision to reported GDP (in either country) could flip the outcome. Experts generally see exogenous shocks (oil prices, trade disruptions, or financial instability) as low probability but meaningful risk factors; India's domestic momentum is believed sufficient to weather most shocks before the reporting cut-off.

Historically, once such an overtaking occurs at the top-economy level, reversals are rare unless driven by currency swings, and all experts agree the base rate now favors India—albeit not with total certainty due to possible revisions. Given all this, the final assigned probabilities by experts range from roughly 80% to 93% in favor of a 'Yes' outcome, with the vast majority clustering tightly between 82% and 90%. In summary, experts very strongly—but not absolutely—expect IMF's January 2026 data to confirm India's nominal GDP for 2025 exceeding Japan's, citing structural and cyclical advantages, but they consistently note that thin margins and late-year exchange rate or data surprises maintain residual risk.
